tasks.title: [cloud-early] M2-16 tenant rate-limit key spoofing -- RateLimitMiddleware tenant-key must verify bearer JWT before trusting X-Tenant-Id
tasks.spec:
docs/design/ADR-2026-09-09-B-mvp1-hardening-and-mvp2-scope.md M2-16 (tenant boundary adversarial test coverage: cross-query / privilege-escalation / rate-limit, priority 2). [cloud-early] MVP-2 priority-2 independent module (ADR-2026-09-26-A) -- verified 2026-09-26: cross-tenant data isolation is already covered extensively (tests/adversarial/*/test_cross_tenant*.py, ~15 files), but rate-limit tenant-boundary is NOT.

Concrete gap found by reading src/api/middleware/rate_limit.py, function _resolve_key: for policy.key == "tenant" (used by the "admin" policy, POLICIES["admin"] in src/core/rate_limit/policy.py, limit=30/60s, routes matching /admin/*), the key is built directly from the unauthenticated request header request.headers.get("X-Tenant-Id") with zero verification. RateLimitMiddleware is registered outermost (before RequestContext/auth dependencies run), so this header is trusted pre-auth. An anonymous caller can send POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE to any /admin/* path with a forged "X-Tenant-Id: <victim-tenant-uuid>" header and consume that specific tenant's admin bucket (30 requests/60s) with zero valid credentials, causing real admins of the victim tenant to get 429 AUTH_RATE_LIMITED on legitimate admin actions (silent DoS). This is the exact same class of vulnerability the "subject" branch of the same function already defends against (see the comment above _resolve_key's subject branch: it insists on verifying the JWT signature before trusting a subject id, specifically to prevent an attacker exhausting a named victim's bucket) -- the "tenant" branch has no equivalent protection.

Downstream authorization (src/foundation/trust/application/resolve_tenant_context.py, TenantMismatchError -> 403 AUTH_TENANT_MISMATCH) is unaffected and already correct -- this leaf is about the pre-auth rate-limit gate only, not tenant data isolation itself.

DoD checklist (falsifiable):
- new adversarial test: an unauthenticated request (no Authorization header) to an /admin/* path with a forged X-Tenant-Id belonging to a different tenant does NOT decrement/consume that tenant's dedicated "tenant:<id>" bucket -- it must fall back to the "ip:" bucket (mirrors the existing subject-branch fallback two lines below in the same function).
- new adversarial test: repeating that forged-header request past the admin policy limit (30) must NOT cause a subsequent legitimate, validly-authenticated admin request for the real tenant to be blocked (proves the victim tenant bucket was never touched).
- existing behavior preserved: an authenticated admin request (valid signed bearer JWT) with a matching X-Tenant-Id still buckets per-tenant exactly as today (no regression to tests/integration/api/test_rate_limit_storm.py).
- fix: the tenant branch of _resolve_key must decode/verify the bearer JWT (same jwt.decode call + secret/algorithm already used a few lines below for the subject branch) before trusting X-Tenant-Id; if there is no validly-signed bearer token, fall back to "ip:" exactly like the subject branch does today. Do not add a DB membership lookup here (that would defeat the point of this being a pre-auth fast-reject layer -- real membership enforcement stays in resolve_tenant_context downstream).
- python -m pytest tests/adversarial/api/ tests/integration/api/test_rate_limit_storm.py -q passes; ruff/mypy clean; file stays under 300 lines.

Non-goals: do not touch resolve_tenant_context.py, foundation_deps.py, or any order/money path -- this is PLT-25 rate-limit middleware only.
